clue.text: A tipster's manner is confused and not totally clear

indicators.note: something confused is jumbled up, so the letters of the preceding words are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A racing tipster speaks in a muddled way, so their advice never quite comes through.
explanation.definitionFit: Something only partly see-through lets some light pass but is not wholly clear, which is what the prefix semi- conveys.

clue.text: Captain of slalom team member keeping very quiet?

indicators.note: one thing keeping another holds it within, so the skier word wraps round the quiet letters

parts.note: slalom is a skiing event, so a member of its team is a skier
PP, pianissimo, is the musical mark for very quiet

explanation.surface: A question about who leads a ski team and whether that person stays silent.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's master or team leader is often called by this informal title, a synonym for captain.

clue.text: Like steel cutlery tons used to cut food

indicators.note: a letter used to cut a word is placed inside it, splitting the food word in two

parts.note: a meal is a serving of food

explanation.surface: Steel knives and forks are said to slice through great quantities of food.
explanation.definitionFit: Steel is an alloy of iron, so steel knives and forks are made of this material, used here adjectivally.

clue.text: Strong winds sent a door swinging

indicators.note: swinging suggests loose movement back and forth, signalling that these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gale blows so hard that it sets a door banging on its hinges.
explanation.definitionFit: Twisters are violent rotating storms, among the strongest winds known.

clue.text: A peculiar genus of plants

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or peculiar

explanation.surface: A botanist remarks on an odd group of plants.
explanation.walkthrough: RUM as an adjective meaning strange is old-fashioned British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: The lords-and-ladies or cuckoo-pint belong to this botanical genus, a plant family name.

clue.text: Attractive at first sight with a note of promise, wearing glasses

indicators.note: clothes or spectacles being worn surround the wearer, so the promise note sits inside the glasses word

parts.note: specs is short for spectacles, i.e. glasses
an IOU is a written note promising to repay a debt

explanation.surface: Someone in spectacles looks appealing at first, like a promising IOU.
explanation.definitionFit: A specious argument or person seems plausible or pleasing on the surface but is misleading underneath.

clue.text: Fellow's got under a million in capital

indicators.note: in a down entry, the piece that has got under the others is written after them

parts.note: a fellow is a man; the 's is 'has'

explanation.surface: A man has got by on less than a million while living in a big city.
explanation.definitionFit: This city is the capital of Jordan, so it is an example of a capital.

clue.text: Looking forward to former setter getting good

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
pectin is the substance that makes jam set

explanation.surface: A retired crossword setter hopes to get better at the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' suggests the compiler of the puzzle; here it is the jam-setting agent PECTIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Anticipating something means awaiting it eagerly, the same sense as looking forward to it.

clue.text: Ancient hero of Florida and Alabama?

definitions.meaning: the Athenian who slew the Minotaur
both states lie in the southeast of America

explanation.surface: A query about which legendary hero belongs to two southern American states.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as THE SE US: Florida and Alabama are in the south-east of the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: The Minotaur-slaying king of Athens is one of the great figures of Greek legend.

clue.text: Temporary diversion going all around ruined tel

indicators.note: letters going all around are moved every which way, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A detour circles a wrecked stretch of road, abbreviated tel.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief pause or entertainment between acts is a break from the main business, a temporary diversion.

clue.text: Tree is full with the mass at its head

indicators.note: the mass letter is taken from where it sits and placed at the front of the word

parts.note: ample means full or plentiful
M is the physics symbol for mass

explanation.surface: A tree is laden with fruit, and its biggest bulk is at the top.
explanation.definitionFit: The sycamore and the sugar tree are members of this genus, an example of a tree.

clue.text: Grub, not to provide food and support

indicators.note: not means the following word is taken away from the grub word

parts.note: a grub is a larva, such as a caterpillar
to cater is to provide food

explanation.surface: Someone declines to supply grub and help.
explanation.definitionFit: A column holding up a roof is a structural support.

clue.text: Point small boat across loch

indicators.note: the boat lies across the loch letter, so that letter goes inside it

parts.note: a pinnace is a small boat carried on a ship
L is the map abbreviation for loch, a Scottish lake

explanation.surface: Someone points out a little boat crossing a Scottish lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A peak or summit is a high point, and figuratively the highest point of achievement.

clue.text: Clergyman's a board member after day one?

indicators.note: what remains after the day and one letters are taken off the board member

parts.note: a director sits on a company board
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A clergyman becomes a company director on his first day.
explanation.definitionFit: A parish priest in charge of a church is a member of the clergy; 'Clergyman's' reads as 'clergyman is'.

clue.text: Study text for play draft on Broadway?

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
a script is the written text of a play

explanation.surface: An actor studies the script of a new play heading for Broadway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draft' looks like a first version of a script; Broadway signals the American sense of military call-up.
explanation.definitionFit: In America the draft is compulsory enlistment, so to call someone up is to enlist them by law.

clue.text: Scots town, mostly where there's rubbish chips

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter of the word

parts.note: a dump is where rubbish is left
fries are chips, as Americans call them

explanation.surface: A disparaging remark about a Scottish town full of litter and chip papers.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a market town in southwest Scotland, so it is a Scottish town.

clue.text: Perhaps Cologne newspaper's taken in neighbouring country

indicators.note: the newspaper is taken in by the country, i.e. placed inside it

parts.note: France borders Germany, where Cologne is
a rag is a disparaging word for a newspaper; 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A paper from the German city of Cologne is read across the border in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cologne' suggests the German city, but here it is eau de cologne, a scent.
explanation.definitionFit: Eau de cologne is a perfume, an example of a pleasant scent, hence 'Perhaps'.

clue.text: Ancient area in 1006, a former principality

indicators.note: the ancient area pieces go in the number written in Roman numerals

parts.note: in Roman numerals 1000 is M and 6 is VI
old means ancient

explanation.surface: A historical note about an old region in the year 1006.
explanation.definitionFit: This Danubian principality, now largely Moldova and part of Romania, was a medieval and later state ruled by a prince.

clue.text: Something unlikely in telephoto picture?

definitions.meaning: a bet or venture with little chance of success
a telephoto lens takes a picture from a great distance

explanation.definitionFit: An outsider with poor odds is an unlikely winner; a photo taken from far away is a distant shot.

clue.text: Chap keeping bar in Mediterranean country

indicators.note: the chap keeping something holds it inside his name

parts.note: Leon is a man's name
to bar is to ban

explanation.surface: A man who runs a bar somewhere around the Mediterranean.
explanation.definitionFit: This nation lies on the eastern shore of the Mediterranean Sea, beside Syria and Israel.

clue.text: Suspend inhibition

definitions.meaning: to hang something up is to suspend it from a hook

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb phrase it means to hang from a hook; as a noun it is a psychological complex or block.

clue.text: In favour of support involving key pupil

parts.note: pro means in favour of

indicators.note: the support involves the key, meaning it takes the key letter inside

parts.note: a tee is a peg supporting a golf ball
G is a musical key

explanation.surface: Someone who favours supporting a key student.
explanation.definitionFit: A person guided by a patron or mentor is a pupil of sorts.

clue.text: Support team that's bottom

parts.note: to back is to support
a side is a team

explanation.surface: Backing a team that is at the bottom of the league.
explanation.definitionFit: The buttocks are a person's rear end, also called the bottom.

clue.text: Perhaps note authority for decision

parts.note: say means for example, perhaps
so (soh) is a note in the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Perhaps a written note gives the authority for a decision.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the final word or permission on a matter means having the authority to decide it.

clue.text: Quick break from work in Post Office

indicators.note: the break is placed in the post office letters

parts.note: a rest is a break from work

explanation.surface: A worker takes a short break in the Post Office.
explanation.definitionFit: In music this tempo marking means fast, and generally it means quickly, as in a magician's call.

clue.text: Fast computer link nearly installed in street

indicators.note: the link is installed inside the street letters
nearly means without the last letter

parts.note: Wi-Fi is a wireless computer connection

explanation.surface: A speedy computer connection has almost been installed along the street.
explanation.definitionFit: Quick and rapid are synonyms of this adjective, meaning fast.

clue.text: Spot line included in autonomous program

indicators.note: the line letter is included inside the program word

parts.note: a bot is software that runs automatically on its own

explanation.surface: A spot or line appears in a computer program running by itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A stain or blemish is a spot, such as an ink mark.

clue.text: Misyoke with this makes donkey very vocal

parts.note: split the answer as ...: misyoke with ... left becomes moke, a donkey

explanation.surface: Wrongly harnessing a donkey makes it bray loudly.
explanation.walkthrough: MOKE is British slang for a donkey. Remove I, S and Y from MISYOKE and MOKE is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Loud and clamorous, making plenty of sound, is the sense of being very vocal.

clue.text: Potential lover of beer not heartlessly cutting source of wine

indicators.note: the beer pieces cut into the vine, splitting it

parts.note: grapes come from the vine
ale is a type of beer

indicators.note: heartlessly means with the middle letter of the word removed

explanation.surface: A would-be lover prefers wine to beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweetheart chosen on 14 February is a person one may love, a potential lover.

clue.text: Newspaper operations room where one can go to play

definitions.text: where one can go to play

parts.note: a national is a newspaper sold across the whole country
an operating theatre is a room for surgery

explanation.surface: A newspaper office houses an operations room for the staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' looks like recreation, but here it is a stage play; the venue is London's state-funded theatre on the South Bank.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre is a venue to see drama, so it is where one goes to watch a play.
